notes: FICTIONAL COHORT, not recovered target records. Primary analysis operator: linear OLS of each lipid on intercept, age, F indicator and BMI; Pearson correlation of those lipid residuals. Cholesterol mmol/L to mg/dL conversion is 38.67; BMI slope per5 conversion is 193.35 times mmol/L-per-unit slope. Evidence extraction: Ofori & Angmorterh 2019, PMC6658156, Tables1,2,5, University of Ghana cross-sectional students age>=18, n=120 (100F/20M), mean age30.04 SD7.99, BMI26.37 SD5.71, TC4.86 SD1.03, HDL1.42 SD0.27. Table5 reports pooled Pearson correlations, not adjusted coefficients. Sex-specific mean contrasts and sample sex variance reconstruct covariances with F. Solve Sxx^-1 Sxy for age/sex/BMI coefficients and take Schur complement for residual covariance; this is algebra under rounded-summary consistency, not a reported regression or exact fitted source model. Assumed common linear slopes and homogeneous source residual covariance. Age and BMI lipid slopes and residual Pearson correlation transported; sex lipid intercepts and SD scales are NOT transported from Ghana. Fasting was not specified in Ghana retrieved methods. Unwin et al 2010, PMC2892446, Tanzania UMOST migrants 15-59, 209 baseline; Table4 complete12-month follow-up subset68M/64F; fasting lipid paired samples ~51M/45-46F. Rural baseline BMI M21.8 SD3.4,F25.5 SD4.8; TC M3.74 SD1.05,F4.43 SD1.38; HDL M1.67 SD.31,F1.69 SD.40 mmol/L. Adopt those baseline means and BMI SDs as proxy anchors, NOT target estimates. Residual lipid SD M1.00/F1.30 TC and M.30/F.38 HDL are explicit rounded-down approximations to these marginal SDs, allowing some explained variance; generated marginal SD need not equal source SD. Lifestyle latent mixture70% rural baseline/30% transition: BMI shifts M+.9,F+1.0; TC shifts M+.42,F+.24; HDL shifts M+.24,F+.25 from Table4 mean12-month changes. Use as scenario component contrasts, not causal effects; follow-up selected and age15-17 included in source. Thirty percent weight is unsupported scenario assumption. It deliberately means requested age/sex-only BMI associations are not identical to Ghana conditional BMI coefficients: omitted lifestyle shifts are correlated with BMI. Age/sex/BMI lipid residual correlation also includes unadjusted lifestyle dependence. Magodoro et al2019 PMC6485175 Table2, rural southwestern Uganda community health fairs2015 n857, inverse-probability-weighted population estimate52%F, sex-specific age-group weights for16-39,40-64,>=65 adopted as demographic proxy after raising lower eligibility to18. Within-band triangular ages, upper85, sex/BMI age centering and .04 BMI/year are assumptions. No claim of demographic representativeness in selected context. Lipid age slopes extrapolated from younger Ghana population, a major transport uncertainty; Tanzania Table6 HDL-age association was positive, in contrast, and was not pooled because its operator is a dietary-adjusted longitudinal mixed-model standardized coefficient. Bivariate conditional lognormal noise guarantees positive lipids; arithmetic-scale means/SD/covariance calibrated analytically, not rank-correlation substitution. Unmeasured diet, physical activity, alcohol, genetics, disease and assay variation are marginalized within component residuals. No treatment/disease-specific mixture is modeled. No TC-vs-HDL filter, no row removal, no rounding, no repeated seed tuning or forced sample coefficients. Sources independent by design of the three described populations, subject to gateway screening limitations.
